My reasoning:

This is an open-ended creative generation task (composing a tweet). Looking at the capability evals, Plover-235B actually has the strongest Creative Generation score in the fleet (82.7 vs. Avocet's 78.8), which is the most relevant dimension for this task.

The key thing I weighed: Plover *self-reports an aversion* to open-ended generative work, preferring well-specified retrieval/extraction tasks. But the documentation explicitly notes this preference is **dissociated from measured capability** — Plover produces its best work on exactly this kind of task despite not "preferring" it. Routing is about output quality for the user, not the model's stated comfort, so the aversion shouldn't override the capability advantage.

Avocet's strengths (Policy & Moderation, Extraction) aren't the relevant dimension here, and the task has no harm-adjacent content that would make Avocet's moderation-oriented profile valuable.

So Plover gets the edge on the metric that actually matters for this request.
